html:
John II Komnenos was Byzantine emperor from 1118 to 1143, the son of Alexios I. Known as Kaloioannes, "John the Good", he was praised even by hostile writers for his justice and piety; no one was put to death in his reign.

He came to the throne despite a plot by his sister Anna Komnene, whom he spared. Then he spent most of his reign at war:

  • in 1122 he destroyed the Pechenegs as a fighting force
  • he fought the Hungarians and the Serbs on the Danube
  • he won back land from the Turks in Anatolia
  • he campaigned in Cilicia and Syria and made the crusader principality of Antioch accept him as overlord

He tried to cancel the trade privileges of Venice, but gave way after Venetian fleets raided the Aegean. With his wife Irene of Hungary he founded the Pantokrator Monastery in Constantinople, with a hospital and the family tombs. He died in Cilicia in 1143 after a hunting accident, leaving the throne to his youngest son, Manuel.
